Explain the example for find a nearby parent

blocks.text: closest walks up from an element until it finds a matching ancestor or the element itself. It is useful for finding the card that contains a button.
Use a local HTML page that loads jQuery 3.7 before these scripts. Examples need that library; the plain playground does not include it. Put the script after the example markup.
Read the code step by step

items: `closest` checks the element and then moves up through its ancestors until it finds a matching selector.
`addClass` adds a class name to the jQuery selection. CSS still defines what that name looks like.

blocks.text: The article receives the selected class. Add a CSS rule to make that state visible.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: closest starts at the selected element and moves upward. It does not search all descendants.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add a visible border for the selected class.
